text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jordan welcomes U.S. announcement that it intends to increase aid to Jordan. Officials expect aid to reach $100 million this year.
- Royal decree on election law reallocates seats in Jordan's 12 provinces. No change in total of 80 parliamentary seats.
- Health Ministry committee completes plan for comprehensive health programme for pre-school children.
- Cabinet expected to discuss on Saturday increases in military and civilian pensions, and increase in ceiling on aid to poor.
- Government expected to push forward with tough amendments to press and publications law.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says government looking into cutting administrative red tape, but no plans for secret committee to monitor performance of government employees.
- All accounts of Amman Bank for Investment, due to be taken over by Arab Bank, to be closed this week.
- U.S. aid to Jordan will be increased, State Department spokesman says.
- Ministry of Interior asks political parties to submit annual budgets for inspection.
